_comment: Golden set v2 floors (the Phase 14.0 plan, section 14.0 / P14-D4). Recorded by block 14-A2 (T14.0.5). T14.2.8 (block 14-C2) turns enforcement on PER METRIC (the `enforce` object below) instead of 14-A2's single global `enforce_now` switch: a metric is enforced once its floor is both in force (14.2 onward, i.e. every floor here) and actually met by the measured numbers; `enforce_now` is kept only as a human-readable note of when enforcement as a concept started, no longer read by gate.py.
_enforce_comment: block 14-C2 (T14.2.8): noisy_recall (1.000), greeting_reply_p95_s (~1.48s) and router_p95_s (~1.05s local) enforced from that block. Block 14-C3 (T14.2.9, DEC-062) adds follow_up_resolution: measured 0.900 on BOTH final verification runs (gate-20261125T130554Z-2888977.log and gate-20261125T131222Z-2925883.log, --only eval, n=10 follow-up turns after this block's +4 dialogues) -- clears the 0.85 floor reliably, not a one-off, so enforced from this block on. intent_accuracy (0.840 on both of the same two runs, DOWN from 14-C2's 0.873 on the smaller 63-turn fixture) and conversational_reply_rate (0.944) remain below their floor -- recorded, not enforced. intent_accuracy's gap is a router ambiguous-vs-followup boundary confusion on terse, several-turns-back follow-ups (the resolved standalone_query is correct; only the intent LABEL is wrong, which does not affect follow_up_resolution -- that metric keys off the golden set's own expected_intent, not the observed one): block 14-C3 tried a sharper intent definition and a contrasting few-shot example (live-tested against the real router), neither reliably fixed it and one variant regressed standalone_query quality, so the clarified definition was kept but the extra example was reverted; closing this needs router-prompt/model work beyond retrieval-time fixes, out of this block's scope -- see the ADR's '14-C3 decision' section and the block report's 'Needs the user's decision'. Flipping intent_accuracy/conversational_reply_rate to `true` without first raising the real number would fail `gate.sh --full` outright.
